plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Plump, ruffled blooms open from fat buds and fill the air with a sweet, rosy perfume. The flowers sit above glossy, deeply cut leaves. Each plant puts on a lavish show in the late-spring garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (roughly May to early June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, including the American Midwest and northern Europe; native to northern China and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies are long-lived perennials. A well-sited clump can bloom for decades, and some have outlasted the gardeners who planted them.

plants.name: Rhododendron ponticum
plants.description: Dome-shaped clusters of bell-like lilac-pink flowers, freckled with golden-brown spots, light up dark evergreen foliage. In full bloom, whole woodland slopes look washed in purple.
plants.location: Woodlands and estates across the British Isles, where it is widely naturalised; native to the Iberian Peninsula, the Black Sea region and the Caucasus
plants.funFact: Brought to Britain as an ornamental in the 18th century, it now spreads so aggressively that it is treated as an invasive species in many woodlands.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A graceful, airy shrub whose silky, open flowers brighten the cool days of the Southern Hemisphere autumn. Golden stamens crown petals in white, pink and deep red. Petals often drift to the ground like confetti.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (late May falls in the Southern Hemisphere autumn)
plants.location: Gardens across southern Australia; native to Japan and China
plants.funFact: This is one of the earliest camellias to flower. Its blooms arrive when most other garden shrubs are winding down for the year.
